subject: Q3 sprintback: metrics readiness and actions for QBR
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Horizon Analytics <ops@horizon-analytics.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Oct 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Q3 sprintback: metrics readiness and actions for QBR

Team — attaching the latest draft Q3 KPI dashboard (Q3_metrics_draft_v3.xlsx) for the leadership readout with Horizon on Friday. High-level signals to call out before we finalize: 

- Latency: P50 up ~9% vs last month, P95 up ~22% (largest deltas for smaller models on burst traffic).
- Cost: unit cost per 1M tokens up ~12% due to higher long-tail token generation and less effective KV cache hit rate.
- Uptime: 99.98% over the quarter; we missed the 99.99% target by ~0.01% (several short infra rollbacks early Sep).
- Usage: active customer token volume +18% M/M; Horizon traffic spikes accounted for ~7% of that uplift.

Asks: please validate the numbers in the sheet and confirm one-line mitigations we can include in the exec one-pager. Proposed owners: latency -> Markus, cost -> Kimberly, uptime -> Irene, usage/forecast -> Marissa.

Also attaching latency delta graphs (latency-delta-graphs.pdf) for model-by-model breakdown. Jonas

Attachments: Q3_metrics_draft_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet), latency-delta-graphs.pdf (pdf)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>

- Kimberly: can you produce a 1-slide cost rollback scenario (cache tuning vs quantization) and expected $/1M token delta?

I'll pull the exec summary into a single slide after the call and post the Drive link to the final slide deck. We should avoid scheduling any risky infra rollouts before the Horizon readout on Friday.

On Wed, Oct 4, 2028 at 8:12 AM Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team — attaching the latest draft Q3 KPI dashboard (Q3_metrics_draft_v3.xlsx) for the leadership readout with Horizon on Friday. High-level signals to call out before we finalize: 
>
> - Latency: P50 up ~9% vs last month, P95 up ~22% (largest deltas for smaller models on burst traffic).
>
Thanks for the summary — dug into the traces this morning. Root causes I see:

1) Incomplete prefix caching for a subset of routes (miss rate ~18% for multi-turn Horizon flows).
2) One kernel fallback on the 2 smallest model variants after a driver update (short windows where we reverted to CPU path).
3) Sudden spike of small, high-concurrency requests from a set of customers (Horizon included) at 03:00 UTC on several days.

Planned mitigations (short window):
- Apply targeted prefix-cache policy change for the Horizon route by EOD tomorrow (expected P95 improvement ~12-15%).
- Roll a focused driver patch to prevent CPU fallback; QAT + canary tomorrow morning (risk low).
- Add a quick rate-limiter rule for noisy customers and tighten concurrency thresholds (will require product sign-off).

I've uploaded latency-delta-graphs.pdf with model traces and timestamps. I'll present the technical summary on the 11:00 call.

— Markus
Senior Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>

Thanks team — good detective work. A few leadership asks before the readout: 

- Executive summary: provide a one-paragraph impact statement we can read aloud (risk, business impact, and confidence in mitigations).
- One-slide mitigation/owner/ETA table — single column each: Risk | Owner | Short mitigation | ETA (hours/days) | Exec-level impact.
- If there's any possibility Horizon will ask for a service credit or special handling, give me the numbers (downtime minutes and affected customers) and a recommended position.

Also confirm monitoring alerts we'll surface in the exec deck: P95 latency trend, cost per 1M tokens change, and cumulative downtime minutes for the quarter. We need a clear ask for Horizon (if anything) — don't leave execs guessing.

Irene Choi
VP, Product Operations | Redwood Inference

Update + meeting notes from 11:00 stand: consolidated action plan and owners below. I've attached the combined workbook (Q3_metrics_draft_v3.xlsx) and the latest CSV export for cost scenarios (cost-breakdown-1Mtokens.csv).

Action items (owner — ETA):
- Prefix-cache policy for Horizon route — Markus — 2028-10-05 18:00 UTC 
- Driver patch canary + rollout to stop CPU fallback — Markus + Infra — 2028-10-05 14:00 UTC
- Cost slide with rollback scenarios (cache tuning, aggressive batching, selective quantization) — Kimberly — 2028-10-05 12:00 UTC
- Exec one-pager + slide (impact statement + mitigation table) — Marissa + Irene — 2028-10-05 20:00 UTC
- Short-term throttling rule for noisy customers (proposal for product sign-off) — Marissa — 2028-10-05 10:00 UTC

Notes: expected aggregate P95 improvement if all short-term mitigations complete: ~14-18% (model mix dependent). Expected cost delta range: -6% to -18% per 1M tokens depending on the path. Uptime risk reduced to <0.001% expected additional downtime for the quarter after the driver patch and throttles.

Next steps: I will create JIRA SUP-3421 to track infra changes and post the final deck link here. Marissa, Kim — please drop the final slide into the Drive link by EOD Thursday.

Jonas Weber
Director, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
